prompt: How many atoms are in the ring of the product formed when 2,5-hexanedione, a 1,4-diketone, is treated with base?
explanation: Base treatment of a 1,4-diketone such as 2,5-hexanedione gives a cyclopentenone, 3-methyl-2-cyclopentenone, which has a five-membered ring.

prompt: What product forms when 2,5-hexanedione is treated with sodium hydroxide in ethanol?

choices.text: 3-Methyl-2-cyclopentenone
(2-Methylcyclopropenyl)ethanone
choices.why: That three-membered-ring product is possible in principle, but it is highly strained and isn't formed.

choices.text: 3-Methyl-2-cyclohexenone
choices.why: That is the product from 2,6-heptanedione, a 1,5-diketone.

choices.text: A mixture of 3-methyl-2-cyclopentenone and (2-methylcyclopropenyl)ethanone
choices.why: In practice only the cyclopentenone is formed.

explanation: 2,5-Hexanedione could give either the five-membered-ring 3-methyl-2-cyclopentenone or the three-membered-ring (2-methylcyclopropenyl)ethanone, depending on which enolate forms. Only the cyclopentenone is formed (Figure 23.6.1).

prompt: Why does 2,5-hexanedione give only the cyclopentenone and not the cyclopropene?

choices.text: The steps are reversible, so the more stable, less strained ring wins
Only one enolate ion can possibly form from 2,5-hexanedione
choices.why: Two different enolate ions are possible, one leading to each product; that is the complication the section describes.

choices.text: The reaction is irreversible, so the first ring to form is kept
choices.why: All the steps in the mechanism are reversible, so an equilibrium is reached.

choices.text: The three-membered ring is more stable than the five-membered ring
choices.why: It's the reverse: the cyclopropene is highly strained, and the cyclopentenone is considerably more stable.

explanation: All steps in the intramolecular aldol mechanism are reversible, so an equilibrium is reached. The relatively strain-free cyclopentenone is considerably more stable than the highly strained cyclopropene alternative.

prompt: If the other possible enolate ion of 2,5-hexanedione cyclized, giving (2-methylcyclopropenyl)ethanone, how many atoms would be in its ring?
explanation: (2-Methylcyclopropenyl)ethanone has a three-membered ring, a cyclopropene. This highly strained product is not formed; the five-membered 3-methyl-2-cyclopentenone is.

prompt: What product forms when 2,6-heptanedione, a 1,5-diketone, is treated with base?

choices.text: 3-Methyl-2-cyclohexenone
An acylcyclobutene
choices.why: That four-membered-ring alternative is more strained, so 1,5-diketones don't give it.

choices.text: 3-Methyl-2-cyclopentenone
choices.why: That five-membered ring comes from a 1,4-diketone such as 2,5-hexanedione.

choices.text: No aldol product, because the diketone is completely deprotonated to a stable enolate ion
choices.why: That happens with a 1,3-diketone such as 2,4-pentanedione, not a 1,5-diketone.

explanation: Base treatment of a 1,5-diketone such as 2,6-heptanedione gives a cyclohexenone, 3-methyl-2-cyclohexenone. Intramolecular aldol reactions of 1,5-diketones give only cyclohexenones, not the more strained acylcyclobutenes.

prompt: Instead of a cyclohexenone, a 1,5-diketone could in principle cyclize to an acylcyclobutene. How many atoms are in the ring of that unwanted product?
explanation: A cyclobutene has a four-membered ring. It is more strained than a cyclohexenone, so intramolecular aldol reactions of 1,5-diketones give only cyclohexenones.

prompt: Why doesn't a 1,3-diketone such as 2,4-pentanedione give an aldol condensation product when treated with base (Exercise 23.6.1)?

choices.text: Its very acidic central CH2 is completely deprotonated to a stable enolate
It has no α hydrogens that a base could remove
choices.why: 2,4-Pentanedione has α hydrogens on both CH3 groups and on the CH2 between the carbonyls.

choices.text: Its two carbonyl groups are too far apart to react with each other
choices.why: The carbonyl groups are close together; the problem is the acidity of the CH2 between them.

choices.text: Base adds to both carbonyl groups and blocks them from reacting
choices.why: The base removes a proton; it is the complete conversion to a stable enolate ion that stops the reaction.

explanation: The CH2 position between the two carbonyl groups of 2,4-pentanedione is so acidic that it is completely deprotonated, giving a stable enolate ion that doesn't go on to an aldol condensation.

prompt: How does an intramolecular aldol reaction differ from the intermolecular aldol reactions seen earlier?

choices.text: The enolate donor and the carbonyl acceptor are in the same molecule
The enolate donor and carbonyl acceptor are two different molecules
It follows a completely different mechanism
choices.why: The mechanism is similar; the only difference is that donor and acceptor are in the same molecule.

choices.text: It needs an acid catalyst instead of a base
choices.why: The section's examples use sodium hydroxide in ethanol.

explanation: When certain dicarbonyl compounds are treated with base, the nucleophilic enolate and the electrophilic carbonyl acceptor are in the same molecule, so a cyclic product forms. Otherwise the mechanism is like that of an intermolecular aldol reaction.

prompt: 2,5-Hexanedione is C6H10O2. How many hydrogen atoms does its intramolecular aldol product, 3-methyl-2-cyclopentenone, contain?
explanation: The intramolecular aldol condensation loses one H2O: C6H10O2 − H2O = C6H8O. So 3-methyl-2-cyclopentenone has 10 − 2 = 8 hydrogens.

prompt: 2,6-Octanedione, CH3COCH2CH2CH2COCH2CH3, is a 1,5-diketone. How many atoms are in the ring of the product when it is treated with base?
explanation: The section's rule is that intramolecular aldol reactions of 1,5-diketones give only cyclohexenones, not the more strained acylcyclobutenes. Whichever end acts as the donor, the ring formed has six atoms.
